title: IT / Finance / Security Admin Sync
summary: Weekly cross-functional sync to review year-end billing adjustments, MFA rollout timing, upcoming SOC2 evidence collection, and a chosen maintenance window for private cluster key rotation. Action items include finalizing vendor invoice allocation, confirming HSM vendor questionnaire answers, and scheduling a dry-run for rotation in staging.
topics: Year-end finance adjustments and invoice allocations
SOC 2 evidence collection and auditor ask list
Service maintenance window and communication plan
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: All right folks, thanks for joining. Uh it's the weekly IT/Finance/Security admin sync — I think we have about 30 minutes. quick round of who we have.
[00:10] Priya: Priya here, finance ops, nothing fancy.
[00:13] Alex: Alex from security — joined.
[00:15] Ellen: Ellen, IT support, hi.
[00:17] Leo: Leo, compliance — hi everyone.
[00:19] Jordan: Great, Maya and Samir and I are on. Ok first item, year-end billing — Samir?
[00:28] Samir: Yeah, thanks. So we pulled the usage reports through Dec 15th, there are a couple of outliers — one dedicated pool billed double because of mis-tagging. We're working with cloud billing, but we need to decide allocation to product teams versus central ops. Priya do you have a preference?
[00:45] Priya: Ideally central ops eats infra surprises under $5k, anything above we roll to the product team that requested the burst. This one is ~12k so we need product-side approval. I can draft the allocation email if you confirm owner.
[01:03] Jordan: The burst was from the 'ConvoSearch' team, I think Maya has context.
[01:08] Maya: Yeah that was a test gone wrong — they left a long-running benchmark. I can confirm with their eng lead.
[01:14] Samir: Ok please do, Priya I'll send the invoice draft once we have owner confirmation.
[01:20] Jordan: Next up MFA rollout status — Ellen?
[01:24] Ellen: We're at ~78% enroled in Okta MFA. There are about 30 exceptions — service accounts and a few VMs that rely on API keys. We proposed a phased enforcement: disable after Jan 10th for regular users then handle service accounts separately.
[01:40] Alex: Security wants enforcement sooner but we get the service account problem. We also need to document the exceptions registry for auditor review.
[01:48] Leo: For SOC2 they will ask for the exception log plus compensating controls. Please ensure we capture owner, justification and mitigation.
[01:56] Ellen: I'll export the exception list and add owner columns.
[02:00] Jordan: Great, next — SOC2 evidence collection. Leo, any new asks from the auditors?
[02:05] Leo: They sent a preliminary list yesterday. It's lighter than last time but they want: access review screenshots, MFA enforcement policy, password rotation evidence, and change control proof for infra changes in last quarter. Also they'll want HSM/KMS config for private key rotation — that's relevant to the next item.
[02:25] Jordan: On HSM/KMS, Alex we've been reviewing the vendor questionnaire?
[02:30] Alex: Yes, I started filling the HSM vendor questionnaire for the cloud HSM option and for the on-prem HSM we need a few more docs. There's a Q that's ambiguous about bring-your-own-HSM for private deployments — the auditor uses "HSM custody" wording and sometimes transcriber made it H S M custody, so apologize if earlier notes were messy.
[02:50] Maya: From the ops side, private customer key rotation will require a brief maintenance window — KV cache invalidation and re-encryption of some service tokens; we should pick a low-traffic slot.
[03:04] Samir: Are there cost implications for key rotation? We may see API retries and slight bill increases. Priya what tolerance do we have?
[03:11] Priya: Quarterly maintenance cost is expected; small bounce is fine if we notify finance. Just keep it under $2k ideally and provide a forecast.
[03:18] Jordan: Proposed window: Jan 8th 02:00-04:00 UTC. Thoughts?
[03:24] Ellen: Works for staging dry-run. For production, I'd prefer weekend but that's fine.
[03:28] Alex: Security wants a dry-run in staging and an incident rollback plan.
[03:33] Maya: I'll schedule staging dry-run for Dec 28th 03:00 UTC and invite SEs and SRE on call.
[03:40] Leo: Make sure auditor evidence is captured during dry-run — logs and change records.
[03:45] Jordan: Great. Next, priv infra — we had open item about HSM vendor questionnaire answers, Alex any blockers?
[03:51] Alex: A few clarifications: vendor provided attestation but the question about 'key exportability' needs precise language. For private on-prem deployments, customers ask about BYOK (bring your own key) support; we need legal to review contract language.
[04:06] Priya: I'll loop in Legal. Samir, can we budget for any licensing fees if we shift to the non-exportable HSM?
[04:12] Samir: Potentially yes, that's why we want to understand run-rate. I'll add a line item for HSM licensing in the Q1 forecast.
[04:19] Jordan: Ok. Next item: change control and evidence for SOC2 — Maya, you're owning infra change logs that feed ticketing?
[04:26] Maya: Yes. We're pushing a consolidated exports job from Jira and Gitlab, but there are some mismatches. We'll reconcile and produce sample report for auditors. Estimated delivery Jan 4th.
[04:36] Leo: Good, include PR ids and approver names — auditors like that.
[04:40] Jordan: Communication plan for maintenance — Ellen you'll craft email and status page updates?
[04:46] Ellen: Yep, I'll draft comms and share in the slack channel #infra-maintenance.
[04:50] Priya: Also need finance note for the forecast and cost center shift.
[04:53] Samir: I'll update the forecast and ping product owners for approval on the 12k allocation.
[04:59] Jordan: Any other items?
[05:01] Alex: One minor security note — we saw an unattended S3 bucket config drift that triggered a policy alert; it's been remediated but we should add S3 drift checks to weekly runbook.
[05:12] Maya: I'll add an automated check and a PagerDuty playbook.
[05:16] Leo: For compliance, please keep proof of remediation in the evidence folder.
[05:20] Jordan: Ok final recap and actions.
[05:23] Priya: Quick Q — do we keep the Jan 10th hard enforcement or move to Jan 17th to give teams time?
[05:30] Alex: Security wants Jan 10th but we can do phased enforcement.
[05:34] Jordan: Let's keep Jan 10th for users, exceptions handled by owner review. Ellen will publish exception registry by Dec 22nd.
[05:41] Ellen: Yes will do.
[05:43] Jordan: Maya will run staging dry-run Dec 28th.
[05:47] Maya: Confirmed.
[05:48] Samir: I'll draft the allocation email and coordinate with product leads by Dec 23rd.
[05:53] Priya: Finance will review and approve.
[05:56] Leo: I'll collate the auditor list and send final evidence checklist by Dec 24th.
[06:02] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next week same time unless urgent.
[06:06] (end of recording)
